explain.say: Gravity pulls every drop of water towards the centre of the Earth. Water is a liquid, so its particles slide past each other easily, and it runs down any slope it finds.

explain.say: A river keeps flowing until it reaches the sea or a lake, where there is no lower place to go. That is why rivers always end at the lowest point around.

faq.a: Gravity pulls water towards the centre of the Earth, and because water is a liquid it can flow and change shape. So it moves to the lowest place it can reach, which on a slope means downhill.
Small streams follow the lowest ground and meet in valleys. Each time two join, the flow gets bigger, so many small streams, called tributaries, add up to a large river.

faq.q: Why do rivers flow faster in the mountains?
faq.a: On a steep slope, more of gravity's pull points along the ground, so the water speeds up. Lower down, where the land is nearly flat, the river slows down.
asks: Why is a mountain stream so fast?

faq.q: Can a river ever flow uphill?
faq.a: Water on its own never flows uphill overall. Fast water can surge over a small bump, and in some rivers a rising tide pushes sea water a short way upstream as a wave called a tidal bore.

faq.q: Why do some rivers flow north?
faq.a: Rivers don't follow north or south, only downhill. The Nile flows north because the land in East Africa where it starts is higher than the Mediterranean coast of Egypt.
asks: Why does the Nile flow north?

facts: The Nile flows north for about 6,650 kilometres into the Mediterranean Sea.
A river's slope is usually steepest near its source in the hills and gentlest near its mouth.

quiz.say: Why does the Nile flow from south to north?

options.show: The Earth's spin pushes it north

quiz.why: Rivers flow downhill, and the Nile starts in the high lands of East Africa and ends at the low Mediterranean coast.

wrong.0: Rivers flow in every direction; they simply go downhill.
wrong.1: The Earth's spin doesn't decide a river's direction; the slope of the land does.
